style: Photographed on 35mm with vintage wide primes (18–35mm) and slow fine-grained stock, natural light only — low winter sun raking across the frame, heavy overcast, blue dusk, or the dull orange firelight of lava — mostly locked-off wide establishing shots and slow creeping dollies at ground level, deep focus, real weather in the air, graded to a cool basalt near-black #101214 with restrained natural colour and a single magma-orange #FF7A1A accent where heat or low sun appears, fine organic grain, no stylisation, no fantasy, grand, quiet, real.
collage_style: A clean scientific-illustration collage on a flat basalt-black #101214 field: sharply cut-out photographic fragments of rock strata, ice margins, sea surface and orbital diagrams with soft torn paper edges and faint drop shadows, layered over matte paper textures and flat blocks of magma orange #FF7A1A, muted halftone grain and hairline registration offsets, everything still and graphic and completely free of text, numbers, charts or lettering.
locations: An unnamed high-latitude shoreline of wet black basalt under a flat overcast sky, grey surf sliding over rounded cobbles, distant bergs the colour of old bone, low horizon, no landmarks
The open deck of a research ship in the North Atlantic at blue dusk, wet steel, coiled cable, heaving grey sea beyond the rail, spray hanging in the air, figures only as small dark silhouettes
A crevassed margin of a great ice sheet spilling onto a bare stony outwash plain, meltwater braiding across grey till under a pale low sun, wind-blown snow streaming off the crest
A horizontal-walled sea cliff of stacked grey and ochre sediment layers, exposed at low tide beneath a soft overcast, wet stone darkening upward, thin waterfalls of loose sand trickling from the face
A high interior ice plateau at dusk, wind-carved sastrugi stretching to a white horizon, thin cold blue shadow in every trough, one tiny silhouette figure for scale
A cooled lava field of broken black rock with a slow orange fissure breathing heat into a damp evening, ground-level view, steam drifting low and thin across the clinker
elements: A piston corer tube hauled over the rail, its core of layered grey marine mud glistening wet, held flat and level by silhouetted hands, cold light on the plastic liner
A column of stacked sediment layers seen close and edge-on — pale carbonate bands, dark clay seams, a single thin orange-brown oxidised horizon — read as a vertical timeline of ice and ocean
A lone human silhouette, tiny and dark, standing on wet stone or ice to give scale, always seen from behind or in full shadow, never a face
A low winter sun grazing the surface of cold water or ice, throwing long horizontal flares and a single band of warm magma orange across an otherwise basalt-dark frame
A shallow meltwater stream cutting a braided channel through grey glacial till and outwash gravel, muddy and quick, carrying fine rock flour that turns the water milky blue-grey
A diffuse shaft of sunlight pushing through low cloud onto a flat northern plain, one soft pool of light travelling slowly across empty ground, everything else in cool shadow
